basic_info.name: ACI-BENCH (Ambient Clinical Intelligence Benchmark)
basic_info.description: The ACI-BENCH corpus (Yim, Fu, Ben Abacha, Snider, Lin, Yetisgen; Nature Scientific Data, 2023) is the reference open dataset for AI-assisted clinical note generation: 207 full doctor-patient encounters, each paired with a complete clinical note, built from three encounter styles - virtassist (doctor talks to a virtual assistant using wake-words and canned phrasing), virtscribe (doctor dictates to a human/automated scribe with pre-ambles and after-visit dictation), and aci (natural, unconstrained doctor-patient conversation). Its load-bearing property is that it is the largest publicly shareable full-encounter dialogue-to-note corpus (1302 source tokens / 55 dialogue turns and 490 target tokens / 49 note sentences on average), created by medical experts and released openly, so that note-generation systems can be compared on a common test bed. The clinical notes originated from an automatic note-generation system and were then checked and rewritten by domain experts, and - critically for fidelity research - the original demonstration data contained deliberately injected, conversation-unsupported EHR content that was annotated at text-span level and removed, leaving a corpus explicitly designed to distinguish supported from fabricated note content. It supplies the official test sets used by MEDIQA-Chat 2023 Task B (test 1, 40 dialogues) and Task C (test 2, 40 dialogues) and by CLEF MEDIQA-SUM 2023 (test 3, 40 dialogues), with 67 training and 20 validation cases. It also introduced MEDCON, a UMLS-based medical-concept F1 metric, alongside ROUGE, BERTScore and BLEURT.
basic_info.organization: Microsoft (Wen-wai Yim, Asma Ben Abacha, Thomas Lin), University of Washington (Yujuan Fu, Meliha Yetisgen), and Nuance Communications (Neal Snider); data released via Microsoft's clinical visit note summarization corpus and the wyim/aci-bench GitHub repository
basic_info.status: research. Publicly released and freely downloadable since 2023; no new corpus version was issued, but the dataset remained actively used through 2026 as a standard note-generation benchmark and is now embedded in third-party evaluation harnesses.

technical_features.what_it_does: ACI-BENCH provides the input-output pairs and the scoring machinery for the task of generating a full clinical visit note from a raw doctor-patient conversation transcript. Each record couples one encounter dialogue (human-transcribed or ASR-generated) with its corresponding clinical note, plus metadata such as patient name, age, gender, and chief and secondary complaints. The benchmark supports two generation settings: full-note generation (one model maps the whole transcript to the whole note) and division-based generation (the note is split into SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE_EXAM, OBJECTIVE_RESULTS and ASSESSMENT_AND_PLAN with a rule-based header detector, each division is generated separately, then concatenated). Quality is measured by a multi-axis metric ensemble: ROUGE-1/2/L (lexical), BERTScore (embedding), BLEURT (learned), and MEDCON - the F1 overlap of UMLS concept sets (restricted to the semantic groups Anatomy, Chemicals & Drugs, Device, Disorders, Genes & Molecular Sequences, Phenomena and Physiology, extracted with QuickUMLS) between candidate and reference note. The final composite score averages ROUGE, BERTScore, BLEURT and MEDCON. For Module C the load-bearing relevance is that ACI-BENCH is the de-facto reference corpus for measuring summary fidelity, provides the exact test sets used by the biggest clinical-note shared task, and its span-level annotation of unsupported EHR-injected content is a direct precedent for the absent-versus-present content auditing Module C needs.
technical_features.architecture: A dataset-and-harness artifact rather than a model. Data layer: 207 full-encounter dialogue-note pairs in three style subsets, split into TRAIN 67 / VALID 20 / TEST1 40 (MEDIQA-Chat Task B) / TEST2 40 (MEDIQA-Chat Task C) / TEST3 40 (MEDIQA-SUM Task C). Harness layer: pre-processing and rule-based section-division scripts, baseline implementations, and an evaluation suite computing ROUGE, BERTScore, BLEURT and MEDCON (QuickUMLS string matching over the UMLS concept database). Baselines evaluated in the paper span fine-tuned encoder-decoders (BART fine-tuned on SAMSum, LED, LED-PubMed), retrieval baselines (UMLS-concept and sentence retrieval), a copy-transcript control, and instruction-following OpenAI models (text-davinci-003 and GPT-4). A later 2026 precedent (CAP) layers a dialogue-aware Clinical Atomic Proposition intermediate representation with an optional problem-oriented event-consolidation step before rendering, evaluated on a filtered 197-case ACI-Bench cohort with a GPT-5.1 judge.
technical_features.inputs: A full doctor-patient encounter transcript (human transcription for the virtscribe subset, ASR transcript for the virtassist and aci subsets), and per-case metadata (patient name, age, gender, chief and secondary complaints). Optional benchmark-side inputs are the reference clinical notes used as evaluation targets and the rule-based section boundaries used for division-based scoring. No structured FHIR, vitals streams, images or documents are consumed.
technical_features.outputs: The artifact a system under test produces is free-text clinical note content (full note or the four concatenated divisions), and the benchmark produces numeric scores: ROUGE-1/2/L F1, BERTScore F1, BLEURT, MEDCON F1, and their composite. For Task C (note-to-dialogue) the output is a generated conversation. ACI-BENCH does not emit any coded document, FHIR resource, Composition or Bundle; it is text in, text out, score out.
technical_features.standards_compliance: [uncertain] ACI-BENCH does not conform to, claim, or validate against any clinical document or interoperability standard - there is no FHIR resource, HL7 IPS, Composition, or NRCeS profile anywhere in the corpus or harness, and the note text is free-form US SOAP-style prose with legacy subsection headers. The only standardised clinical vocabulary used is UMLS, and only inside the MEDCON metric via QuickUMLS (concept-set overlap over seven semantic groups); UMLS is not bound to the note text as output codes, and no SNOMED CT, LOINC or ICD coding is performed. Conformance is therefore not applicable to this artifact, and any mapping from ACI-BENCH note sections to NRCeS OPConsultRecord sections would be entirely a MediKiosk construction.
technical_features.offline_capability: The dataset and its evaluation code are fully local once downloaded - the corpus is a static file and the metrics (ROUGE, BLEURT, BERTScore, MEDCON/QuickUMLS) can be run offline on a machine with the UMLS resource. There is no server dependency, telemetry or online API in the benchmark itself; only baseline experiments that called OpenAI models required connectivity. For Module C this means ACI-BENCH can be vendored into an offline eval harness without a data-residency problem.
technical_features.languages_supported: English only. All transcripts, notes, prompts and metrics are English; there is no Hindi, Devanagari, Hinglish or other Indic-language content, and no translation or code-mixed support is reported.
technical_features.deployment_model: A downloadable research dataset plus an open-source Python evaluation harness intended for local or cluster use; it is not a runtime system and has no kiosk, clinic, cloud or edge deployment model. Practical footprint is tiny (207 encounter records), so the corpus and metrics can sit on a kiosk-class machine or a developer laptop; only the optional BERTScore/BLEURT transformer models and UMLS database add meaningful disk and memory cost.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: Baselines reported for ACI-BENCH test 1 (full-note, in the Nature Scientific Data paper): BART+FTSAMSum (Division) achieved the highest ROUGE - ROUGE-1 53.46, ROUGE-2 25.08, ROUGE-L 48.62 - attributed to learning corpus-specific headers and exam phrasing; GPT-4 achieved the highest MEDCON at 57.78 with lower ROUGE (ROUGE-1 51.76, ROUGE-2 22.58, ROUGE-L 45.97). Retrieval baselines were competitive out of the box (ROUGE-L F1 40.47 for the UMLS version and 38.20 for the sentence version), and a copy-the-transcript control scored highly enough on surface overlap to beat untreated LED. The paper's own text states the copy control at 40.47 ROUGE-L F1 with MEDCON 33.30 in one passage and 30.61 ROUGE-L F1 with MEDCON 55.65 in another [uncertain - these two figures conflict across the arXiv and PMC renditions, so the exact copy-control numbers should be re-checked against the published table]. In division-based evaluation, BART+FTSAMSum led the SUBJECTIVE division at 51.08 while text-davinci-003 led objective_exam 55.30, objective_results 48.90 and assessment_and_plan 46.19. Later work on ACI-BENCH: LLaMA-Clinic (ACL Findings 2025) reported 92.8% of blinded physician evaluations rating its notes acceptable or higher, with real-world readiness matching physician notes even for Assessment and Plan; CAP (ACL BioNLP 2026) on a 197-case cohort improved source-grounded semCAP recall from 0.574 (transcript-only) to 0.694 with GPT-F1 near-tied at 0.695 vs 0.703; MedHELM Q2 2026 reported a top ACI-Bench jury score of 4.969 for 'Muse Spark'.
performance_metrics.latency: [uncertain] No latency, throughput or time-to-note figures are reported for the benchmark itself, and the original baseline paper reports none. The only timing-adjacent evidence is from third parties: the CAP work notes an LLM judge configuration and the MedHELM harness documents per-model runtime constraints, but neither publishes a headline note-generation latency on ACI-BENCH. The Nixi AI 2026 German-consultation benchmark (a different corpus) reported 10.8-112.3 s per note depending on model and reasoning settings, which is indicative rather than ACI-BENCH-measured.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: The corpus is negligible (207 records; source notes average ~1,302 tokens / 55 turns per encounter). Running the full official metric suite needs Python plus transformer models for BERTScore (e.g. roberta-large) and BLEURT, and a local UMLS installation for MEDCON via QuickUMLS; disk and RAM cost is dominated by those models and the UMLS database rather than the data. The paper's baselines were fine-tuned on 4 NVIDIA Tesla K80 GPUs (as reported for the related MTS-Dialog study), and GPT-4/text-davinci-003 baselines required API access. No kiosk-class runtime is defined, but the metric harness is far lighter than an LLM.
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: 207 total full-encounter dialogue-note pairs: TRAIN 67, VALID 20, TEST1 40, TEST2 40, TEST3 40. Per-table statistics: source length 1302 tokens / 55 turns on average; target length 490 tokens / 49 sentences on average. Repository wyim/aci-bench: 83 stars, 5 forks, 3 watchers, 9 commits, 1 open issue, no releases or packages. The corpus is redistributed through Microsoft's clinical_visit_note_summarization_corpus and is also packaged inside the MedHELM healthcare benchmark suite and the EnvCommons/ACIBench agent environment (114 train / 35 validation / 210 test tasks in that reimplementation).
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Peer-reviewed (Nature Scientific Data 10, 586, 2023). The paper (1) documents corpus construction from marketing-demo encounters created by 5+ medical experts for virtassist/virtscribe and a certified doctor plus a lay volunteer for the aci subset; (2) cleans the data by span-level annotation and removal of conversation-unsupported 'imaginary EHR injection' content; (3) validates content against real clinical note structure and distributions; and (4) quantifies diverse baselines on three held-out test sets using ROUGE-1/2/L, BERTScore, BLEURT and MEDCON, with BERTScore/BLEURT applied only in division-based evaluation because of embedding length limits. Test sets 1 and 2 are the official ACL ClinicalNLP MEDIQA-Chat 2023 Task B and Task C test sets, and test 3 is the CLEF MEDIQA-SUM 2023 Task C test set, making the evaluation directly comparable to the shared-task leaderboards. Independent follow-up evaluations (LLaMA-Clinic ACL 2025, CAP BioNLP 2026, MedHELM 2026) reuse the corpus with their own judge designs, which is both replication evidence and a caution that absolute scores depend on the metric family chosen.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: ACI-BENCH is the single most important external reference corpus for Module C's evaluation story. First, it is the de-facto gold benchmark for dialogue-to-note summary fidelity and therefore the yardstick a SIH evaluator will recognise; Module C should be able to state its fidelity results in terms this corpus defines (ROUGE, BERTScore, BLEURT, concept-level MEDCON F1). Second, it validates the core decomposition Module C already plans - splitting a long encounter into purpose-specific sections and scoring them separately - because the paper shows division-based generation beats full-note generation by 1-14 points and that some divisions (Objective/Results/Assessment) need different models; this maps directly onto emitting distinct NRCeS OPConsultRecord sections from frozen history slots. Third, MEDCON is the precedent for the concept-recall-style check Module C needs (did the summary preserve the clinically salient entities?), and its seven UMLS semantic groups align closely with the drug/problem/device/procedure concepts an Indian OPD summary must retain. Fourth, the corpus's explicit annotation and removal of conversation-unsupported EHR injections is a methodological template for Module C's anti-hallucination and omission auditing - exactly the 'LLM judges verify presence, not absence' problem. Finally, ACI-BENCH exposes the reference-note variability problem (Assessment and Plan sections vary strongly in format and quality), which warns Module C to fix a best-practice template and score against slot coverage rather than trusting free-text similarity alone.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (a) division-based note generation and section-level scoring rather than one monolithic summary, because it measurably improves information capture and matches Module C's sectioned OPConsultRecord output; (b) a concept-level recall/F1 metric in the MEDCON spirit - bind it to SNOMED CT India / CDCI / NAMASTE concepts instead of UMLS, so the metric is both India-appropriate and terminology-consistent with the emitted FHIR; (c) the composite-score idea (lexical + embedding + learned + concept) to avoid single-metric overfitting; (d) the span-level provenance discipline used to strip unsupported injections, reframed as a per-field 'supported by a transcript span' audit; (e) reporting a copy-the-transcript control as a floor, since high surface overlap from copying is a known trap in clinical summarisation. Adapt: build an Indian, code-mixed, AYUSH-flavoured counterpart because ACI-BENCH is US-English and outpatient-SOAP, and re-express its evaluation in NRCeS section terms. Reject: using ACI-BENCH reference notes as a gold standard for training (they are machine-drafted then human-edited, format varies, and the corpus is US-centric), and any assumption that ROUGE/BERTScore/BLEURT alone certify clinical safety - the corpus was designed after discovering that unsupported content can score well.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: The corpus is synthetic role-play, not real encounters: virtassist/virtscribe transcripts were authored by medical experts studying real encounters and the aci subset was a doctor plus a lay volunteer role-playing from symptom prompts, so discourse realism and error distribution may not match a live Indian OPD. The reference notes are not physician-authored de novo - they came from an automatic note-generation system and were then checked and rewritten by experts, and the Assessment/Plan sections vary in format and quality, so 'gold' fidelity is fuzzy and can penalise correct but differently styled summaries. Size is small (207 pairs; only 40 test cases per task), which makes metric differences noisy and human-eval fragile, and the corpus is English-only. Known data defects are documented: some subsets contain swapped [patient]/[doctor] speaker tags from the ASR process, left deliberately uncorrected, which can misattribute clinical facts and mislead a summariser or an evaluator. The corpus models no EHR linkage (no vitals, orders, diagnosis codes, structured survey data), so it cannot validate smart-link or coded output behaviour. MEDCON depends on UMLS licensing and QuickUMLS matching, which may not be freely installable in an Indian product context, and the copy-control numbers conflict between paper renditions, so any reuse of those baselines should be re-derived. Broadly, a high ACI-BENCH score certifies surface/concept similarity to US-style notes, not ABDM conformance, factual completeness on Indian/Indic input, or readiness for physician attestation.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: ACI-BENCH is a benchmark, not a competing product, so it does not erode any of MediKiosk's differentiators - it is a tool MediKiosk can use. It differs from MediKiosk in every axis that matters for the kiosk: it is a static US-English research corpus with no runtime, no offline sync/encryption mechanism (only a locally-runnable harness), no ABDM/FHIR/NRCeS emission, no physician attestation artifact, no India data-residency concern because there is no live data, and no AYUSH history model (no Prakriti/Vikriti, no Dashavidha Pariksha). Conversely it strengthens MediKiosk: it supplies a defensible, peer-reviewed fidelity-measurement protocol and the exact metric family (ROUGE/BERTScore/BLEURT/concept F1) a judge expects, and its omission/hallucination and section-division findings directly inform Module C's harness. The correct framing is that ACI-BENCH validates the measurement approach while leaving MediKiosk's offline, India-residency, NRCeS-conformant-emission, per-field-provenance and physician-attestation claims entirely unaddressed by prior art.

business_info.license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), explicitly declared in the wyim/aci-bench README and applicable to the data; reuse requires citation of the Nature Scientific Data paper. The evaluation/baseline code in the repository has no separate LICENSE file indicated, so code reuse terms should be confirmed with the authors before vendoring [uncertain]. MTS-Dialog and ACI-BENCH are also distributed under CC BY 4.0 through Microsoft's clinical_visit_note_summarization_corpus.
business_info.pricing: Free. ACI-BENCH is an openly downloadable research dataset and open-source harness with no pricing, subscription, commercial tier or paid access; the figshare deposit is public.
business_info.funding: No venture or grant funding is attached to ACI-BENCH itself; it is corporate-plus-academic research output from Microsoft (Health AI / Microsoft Research) with University of Washington and Nuance co-authors, released as a public scientific resource.
business_info.commercial_status: Unpaid open research resource. It is not a commercial product or service and generates no revenue; it is used freely by academics and, indirectly, by commercial vendors who benchmark against it.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Direct alternatives in the dialogue-to-note benchmarking space: MTS-Dialog (1,701 short conversation-section pairs; same author group), primock57 (57 full real-consultation transcript-note pairs), the MedHELM clinical-benchmark suite (which now packages ACI-Bench as one scenario among 121 tasks), the EnvCommons/ACIBench agent environment (a rubric-scored reimplementation of ACI-Bench), and related generation benchmarks such as DischargeMe and MediQA-Sum/ImageCLEF. Non-public or restricted corpora with which ACI-BENCH is usually contrasted include Abridge (~6,862 pairs), Augmedix (~500 real pairs), emr.ai (~9,875 dictation pairs), Nuance (~802k real pairs) and 3M Health (~1,342 pairs). None of these competitors addresses offline operation, Indian languages, AYUSH history or ABDM output.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: No clinical-system integrations (no EHR/HIS, no ABDM HIP/HIU/PHR role, no health locker, no messaging). Its ecosystem integrations are research-tooling ones: it is embedded in the MedHELM/HELM evaluation harness (with a runnable aci_bench scenario via uv), reimplemented as an agent environment under EnvCommons/ACIBench, redistributed via Microsoft's clinical_visit_note_summarization_corpus, and cited as the evaluation corpus in follow-up model work such as LLaMA-Clinic and CAP. Module C could wire the corpus and metrics into its own offline eval harness but there is no live integration to inherit.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The evaluation ecosystem around ACI-BENCH moved toward LLM-judge and rubric-based scoring in 2026: MedHELM's Q2 2026 (v0.7) leaderboard uses per-scenario jury scores for clinical documentation generation (top ACI-Bench jury score 4.969), EnvCommons/ACIBench scores notes against 10-15 rubric criteria grouped into accuracy, completeness and communication quality via gpt-5-mini, and CAP uses GPT-5.1 as judge with source-grounded proposition metrics. This is a tailwind for Module C, which can adopt an LLM-judge or rubric harness cheaply, but also a caution: judge-based scoring can be run offline only with a local model, and the wider field's shift to cloud LLM judges conflicts with the kiosk's offline and India-residency constraints. The persistent gap remains that no benchmark in this ecosystem evaluates ABDM/FHIR conformance or an Indic, AYUSH-aware summary, so MediKiosk can claim a category the benchmark world has not yet measured.

history.release_date: First released as arXiv preprint 2306.02022 on 2023-06-03; published in Nature Scientific Data volume 10, article 586, on 2023-09-06.
history.key_milestones: 2023-06-03: ACI-BENCH arXiv preprint published. 2023: incorporated as the official benchmark for MEDIQA-Chat 2023 Task B (full-note, test 1) and Task C (note-to-dialogue, test 2) at ACL ClinicalNLP, and for CLEF MEDIQA-SUM 2023 Task C (test 3). 2023-09-06: peer-reviewed publication in Nature Scientific Data. 2023: repository created with data splits, baselines and metrics (final repo state: 9 commits, 83 stars, 5 forks). 2025: LLaMA-Clinic (ACL Findings 2025) reuses ACI-BENCH for a blinded physician reader study, reporting 92.8% acceptable-or-higher notes. 2026: CAP (ACL BioNLP 2026) evaluates a source-grounded proposition scaffold on a 197-case ACI-Bench cohort with a GPT-5.1 judge; MedHELM Q2 2026 adds ACI-Bench as a clinical documentation generation scenario with per-model jury scores; EnvCommons/ACIBench reimplements it as an agent environment.
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: No new release, version, or data update of ACI-BENCH itself occurred in the last six months - the corpus and repository are stable and unchanged. The activity in the window is downstream reuse and re-packaging: CAP (ACL BioNLP 2026, within the window) evaluated five methods on a filtered 197-case ACI-Bench cohort using a GPT-5.1 judge and source-grounded semCAP recall/precision/F1, reporting CAP improving semCAP-R from 0.574 to 0.694 versus transcript-only prompting; MedHELM's Q2 2026 (v0.7) leaderboard (maintained with Stanford CRFM, quarterly refresh) retained ACI-Bench as a clinical documentation generation scenario and reported a top jury score of 4.969; and EnvCommons/ACIBench continued to package the corpus as a rubric-scored single-turn agent environment (114 train / 35 validation / 210 test tasks, graded in parallel by gpt-5-mini). These confirm the corpus is stable prior art rather than a moving target, while the LLM-judge harnesses built around it are the part that changed.

market_positioning.target_users: Clinical NLP and medical-LLM researchers, model developers, and evaluation teams; secondarily healthcare AI vendors and regulators who need a public yardstick for dialogue-to-note quality. It is not built for patients, doctors in the loop, hospitals or governments, though hospital AI-governance groups may reference it.
market_positioning.market_segment: Benchmarking / clinical note generation evaluation - the measurement and reproducibility layer of ambient clinical documentation, adjacent to (but distinct from) ambient scribing products, intake platforms, PHR and FHIR tooling.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: ACI-BENCH positions itself, in its own words, as 'the largest dataset to date tackling the problem of AI-assisted note generation from visit dialogue' and the largest and most comprehensive publicly available corpus for model-assisted clinical note generation, released to make model comparisons possible now that generative models make benchmarking critical. Its stated design goal is to model three realistic modes of clinical note generation (virtual assistant, virtual scribe, natural conversation) and to support experimentation across human versus ASR transcription, so the community can 'understand the current state-of-the-art' and study model weaknesses.
